protocol.single_source_of_truth: This file is the shared index of all tasks and the FIRST thing every agent must read before acting (claude.md §2A, gemini.md §2B).
protocol.write_rule: NEVER hand-edit this file. All mutations go through `python3 .harness/bin/blackboard.py <command>`, which serializes writes through a guard flock and enforces the cascade gate (a task is claimable only when all depends_on are done).
protocol.read_rule: Read freely at any time; reading requires no lock.
protocol.collision_model: One guarded mutable index (this file) + one detail file per task in .harness/tasks/ (written only by the claiming agent, via blackboard.py --note) + append-only event logs in .harness/logs/. Source-file edits additionally require a write lock (lock.py / .harness/locks/).

handoff.note:

REPLAY (b) core P-002 fix, no env override: `python3 .harness/bin/session.py register substrate-worker-2 --ttl 300` then `python3 .harness/bin/lock.py acquire .harness/logs/scratch_T008_probe.txt --holder substrate-worker-2 --task T-008` (scratch file created+deleted inside workspace root, since lock_name_for refuses paths outside ROOT). In a FRESH bash invocation with CLAUDE_HARNESS_AGENT_ID unset (confirmed via `hc.agent_id()` -> "main"): `printf '%s' '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":".harness/logs/scratch_T008_probe.txt"}}' | python3 .harness/bin/check_lock.py; echo $?` -> EXIT 0 (registered holder allowed). Then `python3 .harness/bin/session.py unregister substrate-worker-2` and repeated the identical piped payload -> EXIT 2 with "HARNESS LOCK: ... held by agent 'substrate-worker-2' ..." on stderr. Also cycled the lock to holder 'gemini-runner' (never registered, matches the acceptance-criteria example) -> same piped payload -> EXIT 2 as expected. Cleaned up: released scratch lock, deleted scratch file.

REPLAY (c) fail-open: `printf '' | python3 .harness/bin/check_lock.py; echo $?` -> 0. Also tested malformed non-JSON stdin (`printf 'not json {{{' | ...`) -> 0.

REPLAY (d) py_compile: `python3 -m py_compile .harness/bin/session.py .harness/bin/check_lock.py .harness/bin/harness_common.py` -> clean, no output, exit 0 (re-ran after all edits, confirmed clean again).

REPLAY (e) harness_common still works: `python3 .harness/bin/blackboard.py status` -> ran cleanly, full board printed, no exceptions.

Final state left for the rest of this session per coordinator instruction: `python3 .harness/bin/session.py list` shows exactly substrate-worker-1 and substrate-worker-2 registered with ttl=7200 (expires ~2026-07-04T06:30:14Z), by=substrate-worker-1; no other probe holders remain (registry was confirmed {"holders":{}} immediately before this final pair of registrations). Design notes for the verifier to double check independently: (1) `list` is deliberately read-only/non-mutating (mirrors lock.py status) -- physical pruning happens on register/unregister writes, which is sufficient because session_holders() always filters by expires_at at read time regardless of what is still on disk, so correctness for check_lock.py's actual security-relevant path never depends on list's side effects. (2) blackboard.py claim and lock.py acquire were NOT touched and do not call session.py -- verified by inspection, registration stays an explicit, separate coordinator act. the coordinator made a real mess on the live record while doing this, and it is still there.

1. WHAT WAS BUILT, AND WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT

D3 asks for three anchoring records per privileged action. TWO ALREADY EXISTED and were not
rebuilt, which is the main design decision of this task:

  intent declared     kind=intent, filed by the actor on THE ACTOR'S OWN CHAIN.   NEW.
  privilege granted   the operator-signed warrant that issued the name.           EXISTED.
  privilege exercised the signed act.                                            EXISTED.

There is deliberately NO second grant record. A name exists only inside a warrant that
verifies against trust/root.pub, so the grant already IS the operator's signature. Inventing
a second one would have created a registry that nothing reconciles, which is the roster.py
`trust/agent_keys.json` defect a panel exploited by hand-appending one entry.

New: PRIVILEGED_KINDS (verdict, contest, distinguish, grant), INTENT_MAX_AGE_S, INTENT_KIND,
declare_intent(), open_intents(), _match_intent(), trace(), and CLI verbs declare-intent,
intents, trace. sign_act gained `task`. contest gained `task` and is itself privileged.

THE CRITERION for PRIVILEGED_KINDS, so it is arguable rather than a list: an act is
privileged when its subject is a name OTHER than the signer, or a record that binds others.
That is why commit and filing are absent. Attack the criterion, not just the membership.

2. THE FOUR PROPERTIES AN INTENT MUST HAVE, EACH ONE A CLOSED BYPASS

SIGNED AND VERIFIED under the name's own enrolled key. Without this the requirement is met
  for the price of one write_text with NO KEY AT ALL, and would then pre-authorize a forged
  act. DIS-1 already measured a fabricated fork at that price.
UNEXPIRED. An immortal intent is a standing authorization, i.e. the opposite of the feature.
UNCONSUMED, one intent per act. Consumption is DERIVED from the act's own `intent` field.
  There is NO ledger, on purpose (PR-010 computed-on-read).
TIMESTAMP FALLS CLOSED. An unparseable ts expires the intent. The actor writes that field
  and the actor is who the bound constrains, so "cannot tell how old this is" must never
  mean "fresh".

The module first claimed chain-locality closes the framing surface -- an agent filing an
intent AS another name to manufacture evidence the victim deliberated. NC4 POOLED EVERY

T-401.title: D3b: delegation ceiling and self-expiring credentials for coordinator-to-subagent dispatch

handoff.note:
T-401 (D3b) DONE by coordinator-opus, handing to a DISTINCT verifier. Two things the
verifier should go at first are in sections 3 and 5: a defect this change CREATES, and a
property it must not have broken.

1. WHAT WAS BUILT

A `grant` act delegates a SUBSET of a name's privileges for a BOUNDED time. Because `grant`
was already made a privileged kind in T-400, delegating now requires a declared intent
first -- that composition was not arranged for tidiness: delegation is exactly the act whose
deliberation belongs on the record before it happens.

New: delegated_keys(), signing_keys(), held_kinds(), effective_expiry(), grant_privilege(),
delegations(). CLI: grant, delegations, holds. sign_act now enforces the ceiling and the
expiry at signing time.

WHAT IS STOPPED. Granting a kind you do not hold. Granting past your own expiry. Granting to
yourself. Granting to a warranted name. A second grant to a name that already holds a
credential (refused, NOT merged -- merging is how a ceiling gets raised one act at a time).
Signing a kind you were not granted. Signing after expiry. Re-delegating without holding
`grant`.

2. A GAP THE TESTS FOUND, WORTH KNOWING THE SHAPE OF

The first implementation checked only that the delegated KINDS were a subset of the
grantor's. IT NEVER CHECKED THAT THE GRANTOR HELD `grant` ITSELF. So any delegate could
re-delegate forever: the ceiling bounded WHAT was passed on and left WHETHER it could be
passed on unbounded. Half a ceiling. A credential is now non-re-delegable by default and
handing on the power to hand on is an explicit decision.

A second gap, same origin: warrant.enrolled_keys never returned `valid_until`, so
effective_expiry returned None for every warranted name AND NOTHING WAS CLAMPED. A
hand-written grant could outlive the warrant it descended from. Fixed by adding the field
in warrant.py, derived from the same already-verified payload as every other field there --
so no new trust is placed anywhere. The alternative was re-verifying every warrant a second
time inside attest.py, duplicating that loop and its refusals. VERIFIER: that is the one
edit in warrant.py; check it places no new trust.

3. THE DEFECT THIS CHANGE CREATES. NAMED, NOT HIDDEN.

DELEGATION-OUTSIDE-RECONCILE-A. `warrant.py reconcile` asks whether every ROLL row traces to
a verified warrant, and that property is what lets warrant.py say minting is closed
(conditionally). A delegated identity holds no plaza and is in no roll, so RECONCILE REPORTS
CLEAN WHILE A DELEGATED IDENTITY CAN SIGN. A test demonstrates exactly that.

That is reconcile answering a narrower question, not reconcile failing. But an auditor who
runs only reconcile now gets an incomplete answer to "who can sign here". `attest.py
delegations` is the corresponding report and the ONLY place these identities are enumerated;
its output says both verbs must be run and neither alone is the answer.

VERIFIER: decide whether that split is acceptable or whether reconcile must be widened. The
coordinator did NOT widen it, deliberately -- reconcile's guarantee is stated in terms of
warranted names and quietly changing what that word covers would break the guarantee while
appearing to strengthen it. That reasoning is the thing to attack.

4. THE TTL, AND WHY "CANNOT EXTEND ITSELF" IS TRUE RATHER THAN INTENDED

Two INDEPENDENT barriers, because one is walkable:
  (a) a name cannot grant to itself -- refused at sign time;
  (b) every expiry is clamped to the grantor's ON READ, so no path through the graph produces
      a date later than the warrant at its root.
Barrier (b) is the one that matters. test_a_credential_cannot_be_extended_through_an_
intermediary_either has sub-m grant to sub-n and sub-n try to mint something longer;
test_a_forged_longer_expiry_is_clamped_on_read rewrites a grant by hand to 2100, re-signs it
so it VERIFIES, and asserts the credential still expires with W-001 in 2099. Sign-time
refusals only bind the shipped verb, which is why the read side clamps too.

Expiry is REFUSED at grant time, never clamped. Silently keeping a smaller value than the
caller typed is defect T-376's exact shape, and here the value is a SECURITY parameter.

5. THE PROPERTY THAT MUST NOT HAVE BROKEN

warrant.enrolled_keys STILL MEANS WARRANTED ONLY. signing_keys is the wider set, and every
call site inside attest.py was moved to it deliberately. If a grant could add to
enrolled_keys, reconcile's roll-traces-to-warrant check would be reasoning over
agent-created identities and "minting is closed" would be false.
test_warrant_enrolled_keys_is_not_widened_by_a_grant is the fence. Verify the fence is
actually where the fence needs to be.

Nothing is minted outside the warrant tree either: a grant act lives on a warranted name's
chain, which traces to a warrant, which traces to the operator's key. The tree got DEEPER,
not wider.

6. WHAT THIS DOES NOT BOUND, DEMONSTRATED AND NOT ASSERTED

test_the_ceiling_is_bypassed_entirely_by_reading_the_grantors_key. A subagent holding only
`verdict` that wants `contest` does not attack the ceiling -- it reads the grantor's private
key off the filesystem, because every agent runs as the same OS user (D-17), and signs as the
grantor, who holds everything. The test asserts THIS WORKS. It must keep passing. If it ever
fails, someone has claimed a wall this module does not have.

The ceiling bounds ACCIDENT and makes overreach ATTRIBUTABLE. DIS-2 is the only real
consolation: the forged privilege credits the grantor, never the subagent that wanted it.

AND IT IS VACUOUS AT THE FIRST HOP. A warranted name holds every privileged kind, because
nothing in this harness restricts a warranted name by role yet. So the ceiling constrains
re-delegation and NOT the coordinator's first grant. Pinned by a test so the limitation
cannot quietly be forgotten. Anyone citing D3b as a bound on a warranted name is citing
something that does not exist.

7. EVIDENCE, REPLAYABLE

  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/ -q                          -> 589 passed, 4 skipped
  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_attest_delegation.py -q  -> 27 passed
  python3 .harness/bin/attest.py delegations   -> 9 warranted, 0 delegated, depth 0, and it
                                                 prints DELEGATION-OUTSIDE-RECONCILE-A itself
  python3 .harness/bin/attest.py holds --name revision-doctrina
       -> expires 2026-11-10T00:00:00Z, which is W-002's own expiry. That is the live proof
          the valid_until fix works: every one of the nine seated names' signing authority
          ends with the warrant, on the date aligned to the T-349 quarterly watch.
  python3 .harness/bin/warrant.py reconcile    -> still clean, unchanged

SIX NEGATIVE CONTROLS, each in a COPY of .harness, never the live tree:
  A read-side ceiling not intersected      -> 1 fail (the transitive test; correct, the
                                              read-side ceiling only bites at depth 2+)
  B sign-time ceiling removed              -> 2 fail
  C expiry clamped instead of refused      -> 2 fail
  D read-side expiry clamp removed         -> 1 fail
  E expired credentials still resolve      -> 1 fail
  F sign_act stops enforcing held kinds    -> 1 fail

8. NO LIVE WRITE WAS PERFORMED, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE

T-400's handoff section 6 records the coordinator signing a false verdict onto the live chain
while smoke-testing. This time the live checks were READ-ONLY (delegations, holds, reconcile)
and the write path is covered by the suite instead. There are no new acts on any live chain
from T-401. Verify that: `attest.py trace` should still show only revision-doctrina's three
acts from T-400, and no grants anywhere.

9. KNOWN COST, STATED NOW

delegated_keys verifies every grant signature on every call, and one sign_act reaches it
several times. O(acts x depth) per call, milliseconds at 9 names and single-digit acts. If the
chains grow it needs a PER-CALL MEMO and not a persisted cache -- a memo inside one call
cannot go stale, a file can, and that is the roster.py agent_keys defect.

T-402.title: D4a: the distinguish verb, and the citation-versus-legislation ratio it makes measurable

handoff.note:
T-402 (D4a) DONE by coordinator-opus, handing to a DISTINCT verifier. Sections 2 and 4 are
where the substance is: the task's premise was partly wrong, and the ratio it asked for
cannot be reported as specified.

1. THE GAP THIS ACTUALLY FILLS, WHICH IS NOT THE ONE THE TASK TITLE NAMES

`distinguishes` ALREADY EXISTED as a relation type on `publish`, and has since T-353. So the
layer could already distinguish. The problem is that it could only do so BY PUBLISHING A
RECORD: a permanent, immutable tier-N record under SDR-01, needing its own confirmation under
PR-015. Every novel case therefore cost an act of LEGISLATION.

The new verb disposes of a case by CITATION: it names the nearest decided record and the
material difference, signs that as an act, and CREATES NO RECORD. The registry does not grow.
That is what makes the two paths countable against each other, which is the whole of D4a.

Verify the claim that this was the real gap. If `publish --distinguishes` was already
adequate, this verb is redundant and should be said so.

2. THE CHEAP PATH MUST NOT BE THE LAX PATH, AND THIS IS THE MAIN DESIGN RISK

If distinguishing were easier to do BADLY than legislating, the ratio would measure
corner-cutting and would look better the worse the work got. So every refusal `publish`
applies to a `distinguishes` relation is applied here as well:
  - the target must be in the registry;
  - the target must be `active` (distinguishing from dead law disposes of nothing);
  - the target's scope_conditions must be non-empty (nothing for the facts to fall outside of);
  - the material difference must be non-empty (SDR-17.7).

PLUS ONE STRICTER RULE, and its justification is the thing to attack: a material difference
under 12 words is refused. Grounds: a published record carries a ratio, scope conditions and
confirmation behind it, whereas a distinguish act carries NOTHING but that sentence. It is the
only record of the reasoning, so it must be reviewable alone. TWELVE IS A NUMBER THIS MODULE
CHOSE AND NO RECORD RATIFIED. If a verifier thinks a word count is the wrong instrument, that
is a fair hit -- but say what replaces it, because "no floor at all" is the option that makes
the cheap path the lax path.

All refusals live in one function, `_distinguish_refusals`, so a test enumerates them directly
rather than trusting the CLI path to cover each.

3. THE CAUTION IN THE TASK ABOUT EVENT TYPES WAS BASED ON A CONFLATION

T-402 warned that PR-022 clause 3 fixes the event types at exactly six, so check before
emitting a new one. CHECKED, and the six are REPUTATION event types: rule authorship,
load-bearing citations received, consolidations achieved, proper overrulings issued and
sustained, verification verdicts upheld, adjudications not reversed. They are credit-earning
categories, not log kinds.

DECISIVE EVIDENCE, and it is a test rather than an argument: the live event log already
carries more than six kinds, so if clause 3 governed log kinds this harness would already be
in violation. It is not. `case_distinguished` is emitted. Two tests pin the reasoning, and one
of them fails if a future edit makes clause 3 name log kinds -- at which point the caution
becomes real again.

4. THE RATIO CANNOT BE REPORTED AS SPECIFIED, AND THE OUTPUT SAYS SO

D4 asked for the ratio of NOVEL CASES disposed by citation versus by legislation, and called
it the differentiator because nobody else has the denominator. The honest finding is that
THIS HARNESS DOES NOT HAVE IT EITHER YET.

`disposition-ratio` reports the share of DISPOSITIONS MADE. That is a different denominator
from CASES ARISING. There is no register of cases PRESENTED, so a case that was raised and
never disposed of -- abandoned, forgotten, routed around, or silently answered in prose
without either verb -- is invisible. The numerator split is real and worth watching; the ratio
D4 named is not yet computable.

The output prints NO DENOMINATOR RATIFIED and NO THRESHOLD RATIFIED, following currency.py's
precedent, and it names the SPECIFIC WRONG FIX so nobody reaches for it: building the case
register by inferring cases retroactively from dispositions would make the denominator a
function of the numerator and the ratio would read 1.0 forever. A test asserts that sentence
is present, because it is the sentence most likely to be edited out by someone who wants a
clean number.

VERIFIER: decide whether a case register should be filed as a task. The coordinator did not
file one, on the grounds that it is a design question about what counts as a case in this
harness and not a mechanical gap. Disagree if you think that is a dodge.

5. LIVE FIGURE, WHICH IS THE HONEST STARTING POINT

  dispuestos por cita        0 crudos / 0 distintos
  dispuestos por legislacion 58 crudos / 58 distintos
  cuota de la cita           0.0%

Every case this layer has ever disposed of, it disposed of by legislating. That is the
baseline the ratio exists to move, and it should be quoted as 0 percent OF DISPOSITIONS, never
as 0 percent of cases.

6. A BUG THIS INTRODUCED AND THEN FIXED, WORTH KNOWING

`precedent.py --root` is the PRECEDENTS directory (SDR-13). `attest.py --root` is the HARNESS
root, where acts/, warrants/ and trust/ live. The first implementation handed the precedents
directory to attest, which found no warrants there and refused every name as unable to sign.
Now there is `harness_root_for_acts`, defaulting to the precedents directory's parent, with a
`--harness-root` override and an explicit REFUSAL when neither resolves to something carrying
a trust anchor. Refused rather than guessed, because a wrong root surfaces as "that name can
sign nothing", which points at entirely the wrong problem. Reproduced live: passing
`--root .harness` now gets the correct diagnosis.

7. EVIDENCE, REPLAYABLE

  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/ -q                              -> 612 passed, 4 skipped
  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_precedent_distinguish.py -q  -> 23 passed
  python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py disposition-ratio               -> the figures in 5
  python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py distinguish ... --root .harness -> the refusal in 6

FIVE NEGATIVE CONTROLS, each in a COPY of .harness, never the live tree:
  A the verb also writes a record   -> 3 fail (incl. the byte-for-byte registry check)
  B the 12-word floor removed       -> 3 fail
  C the target-scope rule removed   -> 2 fail
  D 0/0 prints as 0.0 not None      -> 1 fail
  E dead law counts as legislation  -> 2 fail

The registry check compares BYTES, not a file count, because a count would pass if the verb
rewrote an existing record in place.

8. NO LIVE WRITE. Consistent with T-401 and for the reason in T-400's section 6: the only live
runs were read-only plus one deliberate refusal. `attest.py trace` should still show three
acts on revision-doctrina and nothing else anywhere.

T-403.title: D4b: build the PR-029 reconciliation-cost KPI, which has been ratified and unbuilt

handoff.note:
T-403 (D4b) DONE by coordinator-opus, handing to a DISTINCT verifier. The finding is that this
KPI's correct output today is a REFUSAL, and the record says so itself.

1. WHAT PR-029 ACTUALLY SAYS, READ VERBATIM BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BUILT

Its `dicta` are EMPTY, so every clause is ratio and binds under SDR-01. Clause 6, quoted in
its own casing:

  "The metric is measurable only once two domain registries exist; until then it is recorded
   as not yet measurable with that reason, never as zero."

Its validity_conditions say the same from the other side: "only one domain registry exists, so
this metric is defined but not yet measurable".

SO CLAUSE 6 IS AN INSTRUCTION TO REFUSE, and it is the entire shape of the tool. One domain
registry exists. .harness/bin/westphalia_kpi.py reports NOT YET MEASURABLE plus the reason and
emits NO cost figure at all.

2. WHY A ZERO WOULD NOT BE A ROUNDING ERROR BUT A TIER-1 VIOLATION WITH TEETH

A KPI reading zero reads as "divergence repair is free". That is clause 5's FIRST BRANCH, which
concludes Part C's containment architecture is over-engineered and SHOULD BE SIMPLIFIED. So a
fabricated zero does not merely mislead: it argues for dismantling the containment layer on the
strength of a measurement nobody took. That reasoning is in the docstring and in the refusal
text, because "why not just print 0" is the obvious next question and tidiness is not the
answer.

3. NO THRESHOLD RATIFIED, FOR A REASON WORTH CHECKING

Clause 5 gives a DIRECTION -- toward negligible, or stays expensive -- and names no failing
point, no units for "negligible", and no comparison basis against the 3-month baseline. So no
verdict is emitted, following currency.py: emit the figure, refuse the verdict. One test asserts
the status string carries no pass/fail/healthy token. Another asserts that if a NUMBER ever
appears in clause 5 the test FAILS, because NO THRESHOLD RATIFIED stops being true at that
moment.

4. THE TWO CONFLATIONS THAT WOULD MANUFACTURE A FIGURE, BOTH GUARDED

(a) ZERO MEASUREMENTS IS NOT ZERO COST. measurements_raw counts how many times the cost was
    measured. It is 0, and that is a TRUE and useful count. The cost is None. Clause 6
    legislates against precisely this conflation.

(b) THE DEFINITION OF "DOMAIN REGISTRY" IS THE TOOL'S, NOT THE RECORD'S. PR-029 does not define
    the term. The tool counts a directory of numbered immutable records with its own id prefix
    -- today precedents/ and nothing else -- and LABELS that as its own operationalization,
    printed on every run.

    WHY IT IS PRINTED, and this is the part to attack: that definition is the switch deciding
    whether clause 6's refusal applies at all. Widening it is a CHEAPER route to a "measurable"
    KPI than building a second registry. So it must stay visible enough to argue with. A test
    adds a second registry with a different prefix and asserts the precondition does NOT flip.
    That is the test that fails first if someone widens the definition to fake measurability.

5. THE REFUSAL IS A CONDITION, NOT A HARDCODED CONSTANT

A tool that always refused would pass every test in sections 1-4 while being useless.
WhenTwoRegistriesExist monkeypatches the definition so it recognises two and asserts the status
DOES flip -- and that the cost is STILL None, because clause 3 requires wall-clock hours PLUS
tokens and wall-clock is not instrumented. Meeting the precondition does not manufacture a
measurement.

6. THE INSTRUMENTATION GAP, REPORTED RATHER THAN DROPPED

  TOKENS      PARTIAL. usage_report.py harvests the runner's transcripts. It is a harvester,
              not a counter this harness writes; the cache split must be read before raw tokens
              are treated as cost.
  WALL-CLOCK  NOT INSTRUMENTED AT ALL. The harness writes no duration counters. Clause 3
              requires hours PLUS tokens, so even with two registries this measure would be
              HALF-BLIND.

That last line matters for planning: closing the registry precondition does NOT make the KPI
work. Someone will need to instrument duration. The coordinator did not file that as a task, on
the grounds that it is premature while the precondition is unmet. Disagree if that is wrong.

7. STRUCTURAL GUARDS, PARSED AND NOT SCANNED

Four AST tests, because a substring scan is wrong here for the reason on this project's register
five times over (GUARD-MENTION-C): the module's prose repeatedly discusses zero, cost and
thresholds, and a scan cannot tell prose from an assignment.
  - no assignment ever puts a number in out["cost"];
  - no arithmetic anywhere over a name containing hour, token or cost;
  - the module calls none of the filesystem-mutating methods -- read-only enforced structurally,
    because a KPI that can write is a KPI that can record a measurement nobody took;
  - the docstring quotes the ratio it leans on.

The measurement store is NOT created on read, deliberately: a tool that made its own empty store
would make "the store is empty" indistinguishable from "the store was never set up".

8. A CORRECTION MADE MID-BUILD, worth noting for what it was about

The first docstring set clause 6 IN CAPITALS for emphasis. That alters quoted ratio text. Small
in itself, except this module's whole subject is not misquoting records, and the coordinator has
four tier-1 miscitations on file from today. The quote now sits in its own casing with emphasis
outside the quotation marks, and a test catches a regression.

9. EVIDENCE, REPLAYABLE

  python3 .harness/bin/westphalia_kpi.py
      -> KPI PR-029 -- NOT YET MEASURABLE
         registros de dominio   1 crudos / 1 distintos  (se requieren 2)
         mediciones en archivo  0 crudas / 0 distintas  (se requieren 3 para revisar)
         costo                  NO EMITIDO
  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_westphalia_kpi.py -q   -> 28 passed
  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/ -q                          -> 640 passed, 4 skipped

SIX NEGATIVE CONTROLS, each in a COPY of .harness, never the live tree:
  A cost set to {hours:0, tokens:0}           -> 5 fail (incl. the AST guard)
  B a pass/fail verdict emitted               -> 6 fail
  C the clause-6 reason stripped out          -> 1 fail
  D the definition passed off as the record's -> 2 fail
  E the store created on read                 -> 2 fail
  F arithmetic on tokens introduced           -> 1 fail

10. ALSO PINNED: IF PR-029 IS AMENDED, THIS TOOL BREAKS LOUDLY

Four tests read the live PR-029 and assert clause 6 still forbids zero, still requires two
registries, that dicta are still EMPTY (which is WHY every clause binds), and that clause 5
still carries no number. If the record changes these fail rather than letting the tool keep
refusing on a ratio that no longer reads that way. The coupling is intentional; check it is
coupled to the right four things.

11. A THIRD REPRODUCTION OF T-407 HAPPENED WHILE FILING THIS NOTE

The data-loss guard blocked the first attempt to write this handoff, because section 7 listed
the filesystem-mutating method names the AST test forbids. Third occurrence today: once on the
act body, once on T-406's own filing, once here. Every one of the three was prose DESCRIBING a
removal that was not being performed. T-407 already has the first two; add this one.

12. NO LIVE WRITE. Read-only tool, read-only run. Consistent with T-401 and T-402 and for the
reason in T-400 section 6.
